title: A Average of Averages
statementMd:
Average of Averages
      Input file:         standard input
      Output file:        standard output
      Time limit:         2 seconds
      Memory limit:       1024 megabytes

The average of averages is not always the average.
VegiCat has just learned about segment trees and wants to practice using them.
For a positive integer n, he considers the sequence ai = i (1 ≤ i ≤ n). He decides to build a segment tree
to answer range average queries on this sequence.
In VegiCat’s segment tree, each node corresponds to an interval [l, r] and stores a value vl,r , which VegiCat
intends to represent the average over that interval. The root corresponds to the entire interval [1, n].
However, VegiCat mistakenly assumes that a parent interval’s average always equals the average of the
values stored in its two child nodes. Therefore, he adds the values stored in the two child nodes and divides
the sum by 2.
VegiCat first constructs the segment tree by calling Build(1, n). After the segment tree has been built, he
answers a query for an interval [L, R] by calling Query(1, n, L, R). The two recursive procedures are given
in Algorithm 1.

Algorithm 1 Build and Query

 2:    if l = r then
 3:         vl,l ← al
 4:         return
 5:    end if        

 7:    Build(l, m)
 8:    Build(m + 1, r)

10: end procedure


11: procedure Query(l, r, L, R)
12:    if L ≤ l and r ≤ R then
13:        return vl,r
14:    end if      
               l+r
15:    m←
                2
16:    if R ≤ m then
17:        return Query(l, m, L, R)
18:    else if L > m then
19:        return Query(m + 1, r, L, R)
20:    end if
21:    x ← Query(l, m, L, R)
22:    y ← Query(m + 1, r, L, R)
                x+y
23:    return
                  2
24: end procedure


Although VegiCat’s algorithm is incorrect in general, it returns the correct average for some intervals.
Count the number of such intervals.

All averages are computed as exact rational numbers, without rounding or truncation.

Input
The first line contains an integer T (1 ≤ T ≤ 104 ), the number of test cases. The description of the test
cases follows.
Each of the next T lines contains one integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 106 ), the length of the sequence.
It is guaranteed that the sum of n over all test cases does not exceed 2 · 106 .

Output
For each test case, output an integer — the number of intervals [L, R] for which VegiCat’s query procedure
returns exactly the true average.
